predecessors.name: Maya city-states (Preclassic and Classic)
predecessors.text: Calakmul and its immediate land (Ox Te' Tuun)

successors.name: Maya city-states (Postclassic)
successors.text: 'the capital of a large regional state with an area of about 13,000 square kilometres'

ledger.x: About 411: a king is enthroned at Calakmul.
546: Calakmul's Tuun K'ab' Hix sets a king on Naranjo's throne.
562: Calakmul defeats Tikal and takes Caracol as a dependency.

About 622: the Calakmul page has 'King Yuknoom Chan of Calakmul supervised an event at Caracol in 619' and 'Caracol Stela 22 records the accession of Tajoom Uk'ab' K'ak' to the Calakmul throne in 622', so the overlordship lasted at least to 619; no page dates its end.
636: Yuknoom Che'en II comes to the throne and Calakmul reaches its height.
648: Calakmul defeats Dos Pilas and makes it a vassal.
672: Tikal captures Dos Pilas and its king goes into exile, 'probably in Calakmul', ending the vassalage; the exile ended in 677 'on the same day that Calakmul celebrated a success over Tikal'.

wars.name: Calakmul's wars on Palenque
wars.outcome: Uneh Chan attacked and sacked Palenque on 23 April 599 'with his ally Lakam Chak' and Calakmul sacked it again on 7 April 611; no territory is recorded as held.

wars.name: Calakmul-Caracol defeat of Tikal
wars.outcome: Sky Witness 'defeated Tikal itself and sacrificed its king' in 562; Caracol became Calakmul's dependency and Tikal entered a 130-year hiatus.

wars.name: Calakmul-Dos Pilas war
wars.outcome: Calakmul defeated Dos Pilas in 648 and reinstated its king as a vassal; Tikal captured Dos Pilas in 672 and held it until 677.

wars.name: Tikal-Calakmul battle of 695
wars.outcome: In August 695 Tikal's Jasaw Chan K'awiil I defeated Yuknoom Yich'aak K'ak' in 'a catastrophic battle that saw the defeat of Calakmul'.

certainty.note: The kingdom had no fixed frontier; the 13,000 km2 regional state is a page figure for an undated Late Classic extent.
